garments.name: Angavastram
garments.description: A single length of unstitched cloth draped over the shoulder above a veshti — worn to temples and formal gatherings alike.
stylingSteps: Fold the cloth lengthwise into a wide strip.
Drape over the left shoulder, letting both ends hang evenly.
Adjust so the bordered edge faces outward.

garments.name: Anarkali Suit
garments.description: A fitted bodice flaring into a floor-length frock, worn over churidar — named after a legendary Mughal-era courtesan.
stylingSteps: Wear the fitted bodice and secure at the back.
Pull on the churidar underneath.
Drape the dupatta over both shoulders or pin at one side.

garments.name: Ajrakh Print Stole
garments.description: Hand block-printed cotton in deep indigo and madder red, stamped with geometric and floral motifs using a resist-dye technique dating back centuries.
stylingSteps: Drape the stole loosely over one shoulder.
Or fold lengthwise and wear as a neck scarf.
Let the printed border sit visibly at the front.

garments.name: Bandhani Odhani
garments.description: Tie-dyed cotton or silk dotted in tiny resist-dyed patterns, tied by hand thousands of times before dyeing.
stylingSteps: Drape over the head and one shoulder as an odhani.
Pin lightly at the shoulder to hold the fall.
Let the tie-dyed border frame the face.

garments.name: Banarasi Silk Saree
garments.description: Heavy silk woven with gold and silver zari brocade — the definitive bridal saree of North Indian weddings for centuries.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat, wrap once around.
Pleat the remaining length and tuck at the front.
Drape the zari pallu over the left shoulder.

garments.name: Bandhgala Jacket
garments.description: A closed-neck, buttoned-up short coat that evolved from Rajput riding jackets — now a fixture of formal Indian menswear.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted kurta or shirt.
Button up to the neck for a formal look.
Pair with matching trousers or churidar.

garments.name: Chikankari Kurta
garments.description: Delicate white-on-white shadow embroidery on fine cotton or georgette, introduced to Awadh by Mughal royalty.
stylingSteps: Slip the kurta on over leggings or trousers.
Leave the embroidered yoke visible at the front.
Pair with minimal jewellery to let the needlework show.

garments.name: Chaniya Choli
garments.description: A flared, embroidered skirt paired with a fitted blouse and odhani — the costume of choice for Navratri's garba nights.
stylingSteps: Tie the chaniya skirt at the waist.
Wear the fitted choli blouse on top.
Drape the odhani across the chest and over one shoulder.

garments.name: Churidar
garments.description: Ankle-length fitted trousers that gather into soft folds at the ankle — the standard base layer under kurtas and Anarkalis.
stylingSteps: Pull on like regular trousers, fitting snugly at the calf.
Allow the excess length to gather in folds near the ankle.
Pair with a kurta or Anarkali.

garments.name: Dhoti
garments.description: A single length of unstitched cloth wrapped and tucked around the waist and legs — among the oldest garments still worn in India today.
stylingSteps: Wrap the cloth around the waist, securing at the front.
Pass the loose end between the legs.
Tuck the pleated end at the back waist.

garments.name: Dastar (Sikh Turban)
garments.description: A length of cloth wound carefully around the head, an article of Sikh faith and identity tied fresh each day.
stylingSteps: Wrap the under-turban first for a smooth base.
Wind the outer cloth in even, overlapping layers.
Tuck the final fold neatly at the side or back.

garments.name: Dabu Print Saree
garments.description: Mud-resist hand block printing that dates back to the 12th century, producing soft, earthy patterns on cotton.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length at the front.
Drape the printed pallu over the shoulder.

sections.subtitle: Everyday cloth from the eastern frontier

garments.name: Eri Silk Chador
garments.description: A soft, matte wild silk woven without harming the silkworm — sometimes called 'peace silk', worn as an outer wrap in cooler months.
stylingSteps: Drape the chador over the shoulders like a shawl.
Cross the ends loosely at the front.
Let the natural texture stay visible, unpressed.

garments.name: Embroidered Kutchi Choli
garments.description: A short, densely mirror-embroidered blouse from Gujarat's Kutch region, worn with a full skirt for festival dancing.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted underlayer.
Tie at the back for a secure fit.
Pair with a matching mirror-worked skirt.

garments.name: Faran
garments.description: A loose, long robe worn by Kashmiri women, traditionally in wool for winter, often paired with a headscarf called taranga.
stylingSteps: Slip the robe on over a base layer.
Let it fall loosely to the knee or below.
Add a kangri (fire pot) underneath in winter for warmth.

garments.name: Farshi Pajama
garments.description: Extravagantly flared trousers that pool onto the floor, once worn by Awadhi courtly women for their sheer opulence.
stylingSteps: Wear the flared trousers, letting the excess fabric pool at the feet.
Pair with a short fitted kurta on top.
Walk with deliberate, gliding steps to manage the flare.

garments.name: Feta (Maharashtrian Turban)
garments.description: A bright saffron or red turban tied in a distinctive peaked style, traditionally worn at Maharashtrian weddings and festivals.
stylingSteps: Wind the cloth around the head in tight, even folds.
Shape the front into a raised peak.
Tuck the final end firmly to secure.

garments.name: Ghagra Choli
garments.description: A voluminous embroidered skirt with a fitted blouse and odhani — Rajasthan's answer to the lehenga, often heavier and more mirror-worked.
stylingSteps: Tie the ghagra skirt securely at the waist.
Wear the fitted choli on top.
Drape the odhani over the head and one shoulder.

garments.name: Gamcha
garments.description: A thin, coarse cotton towel-cloth in red and white checks, worn over the shoulder or tied around the head during fieldwork.
stylingSteps: Fold into a long strip and drape over one shoulder.
Or tie around the head as a sweatband in the heat.
Wash and reuse — built for daily wear.

garments.name: Gadwal Saree
garments.description: A saree with a cotton body and a contrasting silk zari border, woven using a unique technique that joins the two fabrics seamlessly.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the contrasting silk pallu over the shoulder.

sections.subtitle: Handloom heritage from hill to coast

garments.name: Himroo Shawl
garments.description: A blend of silk and cotton woven in Persian-influenced motifs, historically a more affordable alternative to Kashmiri kimkhwab brocade.
stylingSteps: Drape over both shoulders like a wide shawl.
Cross loosely at the front for warmth.
Wear over kurta or saree alike.

garments.name: Half Saree (Langa Voni)
garments.description: A three-piece pre-saree ensemble worn by girls transitioning into womanhood — a langa skirt, fitted blouse, and voni drape.
stylingSteps: Tie the langa skirt at the waist.
Wear the fitted blouse on top.
Drape the voni across the chest and over one shoulder like a saree pallu.

garments.name: Himachali Topi
garments.description: A flat woolen cap with a colourful velvet band at the front, worn year-round across the hill state as a mark of regional identity.
stylingSteps: Set the cap flat on the head, slightly tilted.
Position the coloured band at the front.
No further adjustment needed — it's designed to sit securely.

garments.name: Ikat Saree
garments.description: Yarn is tie-dyed before weaving in this resist technique, producing the soft, blurred-edge patterns Odisha is famous for.
materials: Cotton or silk yarn, resist-dyed before weaving
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the ikat-patterned pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Ilkal Saree
garments.description: A saree woven with a distinctive red pallu attached to the body using a technique called tope teni, unique to Ilkal town.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the red pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Indo-Western Sherwani
garments.description: A modern hybrid combining the traditional sherwani silhouette with tailored Western cuts — a favourite of contemporary Indian grooms.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted kurta or shirt.
Button up the front closure.
Pair with slim trousers or churidar.

sections.subtitle: Jamdani to Jodhpuri — precision and pride

garments.name: Jamdani Saree
garments.description: Muslin woven with a supplementary thread technique so fine that no two motifs are ever placed identically.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the pallu over the shoulder, letting the motifs show.

garments.name: Jodhpuri Suit
garments.description: A tailored bandhgala jacket paired with fitted jodhpuri trousers, originally designed for horse riding in the Rajput courts.
stylingSteps: Wear the fitted trousers first.
Button the bandhgala jacket up to the neck.
Pair with formal leather shoes.

garments.name: Punjabi Jutti
garments.description: Flat, embroidered leather footwear with no left-right distinction, traditionally handcrafted and softened only through wear.
stylingSteps: Slip on either foot — they're identical by design.
Wear without socks for the traditional look.
Break in gradually as leather softens with use.

sections.subtitle: Kings and queens of the wardrobe

garments.name: Kanjeevaram Saree
garments.description: Heavy mulberry silk with pure gold and silver zari, the pallu and border woven separately then joined in a signature zigzag stitch.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length at the front.
Drape the heavy zari pallu over the left shoulder.

garments.name: Kullu Cap
garments.description: A round woolen cap with a colourful embroidered band, worn across the Kullu valley as everyday headwear against the cold.
stylingSteps: Set the cap on the head, band facing forward.
Adjust for a snug fit.
Wear year-round in the hills.

garments.name: Kasavu Saree
garments.description: Off-white cotton with a gold zari border, the defining garment of Onam and Vishu celebrations across Kerala.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the gold-bordered pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Lehenga Choli
garments.description: A flared, often heavily embroidered skirt paired with a fitted blouse and dupatta — India's most recognisable bridal silhouette.
stylingSteps: Tie the lehenga skirt securely at the waist.
Wear the fitted choli blouse on top.
Drape the dupatta over one shoulder or across both arms.

garments.name: Lungi
garments.description: A simple tube of cotton cloth wrapped around the waist — the most practical, breathable garment for South India's heat.
materials: 2m cotton cloth, stitched into a tube
stylingSteps: Step into the tube and pull up to the waist.
Fold and tuck at the waistband to secure.
Fold up the hem for ease of movement when needed.

garments.name: Leheriya Fabric
garments.description: Diagonal wave-patterned tie-dye traditionally worn during Rajasthan's monsoon festivals, named after the Hindi word for 'waves'.
stylingSteps: Drape as a dupatta or turban cloth.
Let the diagonal stripes fall naturally.
Pair with solid-coloured outfits to let the pattern stand out.

garments.name: Mekhela Chador
garments.description: A two-piece drape unique to Assam — predating the stitched saree blouse — traditionally woven in golden muga silk.
stylingSteps: Wrap the mekhela around the waist like a wide skirt.
Drape the chador over the torso and pin at the shoulder.
Tuck any loose fabric neatly at the waist.

garments.name: Muga Silk Kurta
garments.description: A naturally golden-hued silk found only in Assam, prized for a sheen that improves with every wash.
stylingSteps: Wear over churidar or dhoti.
Let the natural golden sheen catch the light.
Pair with minimal accessories.

garments.name: Maheshwari Saree
garments.description: A lightweight cotton-silk blend saree with distinctive reversible borders, first woven for Maratha royalty in the 18th century.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Nauvari Saree
garments.description: The traditional nine-yard saree draped in a dhoti-like style between the legs, historically worn for ease of movement during work and dance.
stylingSteps: Wrap the first length around the waist like a dhoti, passing between the legs.
Continue wrapping and pleating the remaining length.
Drape the pallu over the shoulder, tucking securely.

garments.name: Nehru Jacket
garments.description: A sleeveless, mandarin-collared jacket popularised by India's first Prime Minister, now a staple of modern Indian formalwear.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted kurta or shirt.
Leave open or button at the top.
Pair with churidar or trousers.

garments.name: Naga Shawl
garments.description: Bold geometric weaves in red, black and white, with patterns that historically signified a warrior's status and achievements.
stylingSteps: Drape over both shoulders like a wide wrap.
Let the geometric border remain visible at the edge.
Worn traditionally during festivals and ceremonies.

sections.subtitle: Odhani to Onam, wrapped with meaning

garments.name: Odhani
garments.description: A long veil-like cloth draped over the head and shoulder, often tie-dyed, worn as both modesty covering and colourful statement.
stylingSteps: Drape over the head, letting one end fall over the shoulder.
Pin lightly at the shoulder to hold in place.
Adjust the front fold to frame the face.

garments.name: Set Mundu
garments.description: A two-piece off-white and gold ensemble — the mundu (lower wrap) and neriyathu (upper drape) — worn especially during Onam.
stylingSteps: Wrap the mundu around the waist like a long skirt.
Drape the neriyathu across the chest and pin at the shoulder.
Let the gold border fall visibly at the front.

garments.name: Odisha Bomkai Saree
garments.description: A saree combining ikat, embroidery, and thread work in a single weave — one of Odisha's most labour-intensive textile traditions.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the ornate pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Phulkari Dupatta
garments.description: Hand-embroidered in vivid floral patterns using darning stitch on coarse cotton, once made stitch by stitch for a daughter's dowry.
stylingSteps: Drape over the head and shoulders like a shawl.
Let the dense embroidery face outward.
Pin lightly at the shoulder for a secure fall.

garments.name: Patola Saree
garments.description: Double ikat silk where both warp and weft threads are separately tie-dyed before weaving — one of the most technically demanding weaves in the world.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the geometric-patterned pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Pagri (Rajasthani Turban)
garments.description: A brightly coloured turban whose exact hue and tying style once indicated the wearer's caste, region, and season.
stylingSteps: Wind the cloth around the head in overlapping layers.
Shape the front fold into a peak or fan.
Tuck the final end securely at the side.

garments.name: Qasaba
garments.description: A traditional cap-like headdress worn by married Kashmiri Pandit women, often paired with a veil and heavy jewellery.
stylingSteps: Position the cap securely at the crown of the head.
Attach the veil so it falls over the shoulders.
Adjust jewellery to sit alongside the headdress.

garments.name: Quilted Phiran
garments.description: A padded, quilted version of the everyday Kashmiri robe, layered for warmth during the valley's harsh winters.
stylingSteps: Slip the robe on over a base layer.
Let it fall loosely past the knee.
Wear with a kangri underneath for added warmth.

garments.name: Rajputi Poshak
garments.description: A three-piece royal ensemble of skirt, blouse, and odhani, historically worn by Rajput royalty and still central to Rajasthani weddings.
stylingSteps: Tie the ghagra skirt at the waist.
Wear the fitted kanchli blouse on top.
Drape the odhani over the head, letting it fall to one side.

garments.name: Rogan Art Stole
garments.description: Hand-painted with a thick castor-oil-based paste using a metal stylus, practised by a single family in Kutch for generations.
stylingSteps: Drape loosely over one shoulder.
Keep the painted motif facing outward.
Handle gently — the paste sits on the surface of the cloth.

garments.name: Chamba Rumal
garments.description: A double-satin-stitch embroidered handkerchief so fine both sides look identical — historically exchanged as ceremonial gifts.
materials: Untwisted silk thread, double satin stitch
stylingSteps: Fold into a small square for gifting.
Or display flat as a wall textile.
Handle by the edges to preserve the embroidery.

garments.name: Sherwani
garments.description: A long, fitted coat with a mandarin collar, evolved from Mughal court robes into the definitive groom's garment across North India.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted kurta.
Button the sherwani up the front.
Pair with churidar and a dupatta or stole.

garments.name: Salwar Kameez
garments.description: A tunic (kameez) paired with loose trousers (salwar) and a dupatta — among the most widely worn everyday outfits across India.
stylingSteps: Wear the salwar trousers first, tied at the waist.
Slip the kameez tunic on over it.
Drape the dupatta over both shoulders.

garments.name: Sambalpuri Saree
garments.description: Ikat-woven cotton or silk featuring the distinctive shankha, chakra, and phula motifs, each carrying its own symbolic meaning.
materials: Cotton or silk, tie-dyed before weaving
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the motif-patterned pallu over the shoulder.

sections.subtitle: Textures that travel from loom to street

garments.name: Tant Saree
garments.description: A crisp, lightweight cotton saree with a thin red border, woven for Bengal's humid climate and worn daily across the state.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the pallu over the shoulder in soft, crisp folds.

garments.name: Toda Embroidery Shawl
garments.description: Red and black geometric embroidery on undyed cotton, practised exclusively by women of the Toda tribal community.
materials: Red and black wool thread, counted-thread technique
stylingSteps: Drape over both shoulders like a wrap.
Let the geometric border sit at the visible edge.
Worn traditionally during Toda community ceremonies.

garments.name: Angavastram Turban (Pagdi)
garments.description: A broad umbrella term for regional turban styles, each fold and colour once signalling caste, region, or occasion.
stylingSteps: Wind the cloth around the head following the regional style.
Shape the front fold as per local tradition.
Secure the final tuck at the side or back.

sections.subtitle: Upper wraps from the Vedas onward

garments.name: Uttariya
garments.description: One of the oldest recorded Indian garments — an unstitched upper-body wrap mentioned in Vedic texts, ancestor to today's dupatta and angavastram.
stylingSteps: Drape over one or both shoulders.
Let the ends fall freely or tuck at the waist.
Worn over a base garment for ceremonial occasions.

garments.name: Pichora
garments.description: A hand-dyed yellow ceremonial veil printed with auspicious motifs, draped over the bride during Kumaoni wedding rituals.
stylingSteps: Drape over the head during the ceremony.
Let it fall over both shoulders.
Traditionally gifted by the maternal family.

garments.name: Upada Jamdani Saree
garments.description: A lightweight silk saree combining Jamdani's fine motif weaving with the sheen of Andhra's traditional silk looms.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the woven-motif pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Valkalam
garments.description: A garment made from tree bark fibre, worn by sages and ascetics in ancient texts — among the earliest recorded Indian clothing.
materials: Softened bark fibre, beaten and woven
stylingSteps: Wrap around the torso and secure at the waist.
Historically worn without stitching.
Referenced today mainly in ceremonial or theatrical contexts.

garments.name: Veshti
garments.description: A white or cream unstitched cloth wrapped around the waist, worn plain for daily life and bordered in gold zari for temple visits.
stylingSteps: Wrap around the waist and tuck at the front.
Fold up (kachcha style) for ease of movement if needed.
Pair with an angavastram over the shoulder for formal occasions.

garments.name: Venkatagiri Saree
garments.description: A fine cotton saree with delicate zari work on the border and pallu, known for its light weight and intricate temple motifs.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the zari-bordered pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Pashmina Shawl
garments.description: Hand-spun from the underbelly wool of Changthangi goats, so fine that a full shawl can pass through a finger ring.
stylingSteps: Drape over both shoulders for warmth.
Or fold as a stole for formal wear.
Store folded, away from direct sunlight.

garments.name: Warli Print Saree
garments.description: Modern textile adaptation of the Warli tribe's stick-figure mud paintings, printed in white on earthy backgrounds.
materials: White pigment print on earthy dye
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the printed pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Xador
garments.description: The Assamese spelling of 'chador' — the upper wrap of the mekhela xador ensemble, often woven in gold-toned muga silk.
stylingSteps: Drape over the torso, covering the mekhela skirt beneath.
Pin securely at the shoulder.
Tuck any loose fabric at the waist.

garments.name: Gamosa (presented on a Xorai)
garments.description: A handwoven cotton cloth with a red woven border, traditionally offered as a mark of respect on a bell-metal xorai tray.
stylingSteps: Drape over the shoulder as a mark of honour.
Or present folded on a xorai tray as a formal gesture.
Used in daily life as a towel or wrap as well.

garments.name: Yajnopavita (Sacred Thread)
garments.description: A cotton thread worn across the torso after the upanayanam ceremony, marking a rite of passage in several Hindu communities.
materials: Cotton thread, hand-twisted in sets of three
stylingSteps: Worn across the left shoulder and under the right arm.
Changed periodically as part of ritual observance.
Kept visible or tucked depending on the occasion.

garments.name: Yerukala Cotton Saree
garments.description: A simply woven cotton saree from the Yerukala tribal community, valued for its plain durability over ornamentation.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the pallu over the shoulder.

garments.name: Zardozi Sherwani
garments.description: A sherwani covered in heavy metallic thread embroidery, using gold and silver wire techniques once reserved for royal courts.
stylingSteps: Wear over a fitted kurta.
Handle carefully — the embroidery adds significant weight.
Pair with matching churidar and juttis.

garments.name: Paithani Saree (Zari Border)
garments.description: A silk saree famed for its richly worked zari border and peacock-motif pallu, historically woven for Peshwa royalty.
stylingSteps: Tuck the plain end into the petticoat and wrap once.
Pleat and tuck the remaining length.
Drape the peacock-motif pallu over the shoulder.
